Take-off distance available

Declared length of runway plus clearway that is available and suitable for the ground run of an aircraft taking off.

Questions and answers

Questions and answers

What is Take-off distance available?

In this glossary, Take-off distance available refers to: Declared length of runway plus clearway that is available and suitable for the ground run of an aircraft taking off.

How is Take-off distance available used in aviation?

In aviation communication, this term appears in contexts such as: "Hamburg Tower, Lufthansa 842, request take-off distance available for Runway 23."

Why does Take-off distance available matter in aviation?

Take-off distance available matters because it supports clear communication in Flight Planning contexts for Pilots, Air Traffic Controllers, and Cabin Crew. It also connects to aviation training and exam language such as ICAO Level 4, ICAO Level 5, ICAO Level 6, and EASA FCL.055.

Who uses Take-off distance available?

Take-off distance available is mainly used by Pilots, Air Traffic Controllers, and Cabin Crew.

What category does Take-off distance available belong to?

In this glossary, Take-off distance available is grouped under Flight Planning. Related pages in this category explain adjacent procedures, commands and operational concepts.

Where does this definition come from?
